body:
SHIPPED. DQN.learn filled the targets non-taken entries from an untaped forward over the ONLINE net and the SAME states, then ran a taped forward over the same net and states with no optimizer step between them. The two produced identical values; the first was a whole MLP forward over the batch, paid on EVERY environment step. The tape now opens before the target is built so the target loop reads the taped result. BenchmarkDQNLearn -23.0 percent ns/op, -21.4 percent B/op, -13.8 percent allocs.

The benchmark is new and is a per-STEP cell on purpose: measuring through Episode would have diluted it behind the environment and the epsilon-greedy action selection.

GATE: TestDQNLearnSingleForwardMatchesDouble runs both forwards over one agents weights and compares raw bits, after first perturbing the target net so the online and target nets are DISTINGUISHABLE — without that the comparison would hold for the wrong reason. It also caught a fixture bug of its own: the perturbation initially assumed rank-2 parameters and panicked on the rank-1 biases.

COVERAGE GAP FOUND AND LEFT OPEN RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER: substituting the frozen TARGET net for the online one as the source of those target rows does NOT redden the rl package. Nothing pins which net fills them. This is pre-existing, not introduced here — the substitutions correctness rests on the tape argument, which is now tested — but an actual mix-up of the two nets would pass, and it deserves its own test.

STILL OPEN from the three sweeps: classic presort split-finder column-major relayout (640 KB footprint, past L1, with the sizing already checked); classic six static equal-chunk row loops; classic SVM per-element non-inlinable kernel method call; llamagpu headArgmax column walk (needs an in-package benchmark); tensor gatherHalfTyped closure plus per-element invariant branch plus missing dst reslice; tensor RoundToHalfF32 one-line dst reslice.
